Medians rather than means, because one viral post otherwise decides the ranking; computed over each post\'s LATEST observation only, so a post that stayed in the top 50 for four months counts once rather than four times; bucketed by weekday in `Europe/Oslo`, so a post published at 00:30 CEST is not filed under the previous day.  Every `by_weekday` bucket reports `n` (posts with a usable rate) beside its medians — a weekday can rest on one or two posts, and a ranking that ignores `n` will overstate what the data supports.  `source_health` reports the state of the ingest. `ok` — data is flowing. `stale` / `unauthorized` — the numbers STOPPED moving at `last_success_at`, so a recent dip describes the outage rather than the audience. `awaiting_data` — the poller works but LinkedIn has never yet handed over the posts, so the numbers never STARTED: a thin result means the ingest has not begun. `never_run` — the poller is not configured. `last_data_at` is when posts actually last arrived, a different question from when the job last ran.  `last_note`, `last_http_status` and `last_http_body` are written on every attempt, not only on failures — `last_error` and `last_status` stay empty while a source succeeds and returns nothing, which is precisely the state `awaiting_data` describes. `last_note` says what the run concluded and on what evidence, including the control-domain probe that separates a refused token from a collation delay.  `join_health` reports whether the two halves are meeting. Content and performance are joined on an id extracted from each source\'s own URL spelling, so a namespace mismatch fills both tables and joins nothing while every query still returns rows: `matched: 0` with non-zero counts on both sides is that failure, not a backlog.  REST aggregates publicly-visible posts only, so its figures can differ from the MCP tool\'s. operationId: getLinkedinStatsGet parameters: - { name: from, in: query, description: Published on or after this date., schema: { type: string, format: date }, } - { name: to, in: query, description: Published on or before this date., schema: { type: string, format: date }, } - { name: since, in: query, description: Alias for from., schema: { type: string, format: date }, } responses: "200": description: Totals, per-weekday medians, and ingest health. content: application/json: schema: { type: object } "400": { $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest" } "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" } "503": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Disabled" } post: tags: [REST API] summary: Aggregate LinkedIn performance (JSON body) operationId: getLinkedinStatsPost requestBody: required: false content: application/json: schema: type: object properties: from: { type: string, format: date } to: { type: string, format: date } since: { type: string, format: date } responses: "200": description: Totals, per-weekday medians, and ingest health. content: application/json: schema: { type: object } "400": { $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest" } "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" } "503": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Disabled" }  /api/v1/thread-leaderboard: get: tags: [REST API] summary: His own toots ranked by the conversation they started description: "`replies_count` counts DIRECT children only, so it cannot tell a toot that started an argument from one that collected thirteen flat replies.
